Test Description: This test verifies GPIO input and output behavior by enabling output mode for specific pads and checking that input and output status reflect driven values.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Initialize error tracking.
2) If available, enable the relevant GPIO interrupt line in the interrupt controller.
3) Configure the IO control groups to set pads into output mode for the required range.
4) Enable all GPIO interrupts for the first interrupt group.
5) For pads 0–15, drive a walking-one pattern and verify inputs reflect the driven value, then drive zero and verify inputs clear.
6) For pads 16–31, drive the output data field for each pad and verify the output status reflects the driven value, then clear it and verify the status clears.
7) Complete the test and record the final error count.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
- For pads 0–15 driven high, the corresponding input status bit becomes 1; pass if set, otherwise fail.
- For pads 0–15 driven low, the corresponding input status bit becomes 0; pass if clear, otherwise fail.
- For pads 16–31 driven high, the corresponding output status bit becomes 1; pass if set, otherwise fail.
- For pads 16–31 driven low, the corresponding output status bit becomes 0; pass if clear, otherwise fail.
- If the default interrupt handler is entered, the test fails.
- Overall pass if no failures are recorded.

Test Description: Verifies level-triggered GPIO interrupts for active-high and active-low configurations across a range of pins. Confirms raw, group, and system interrupt status handling and clearing.
Remarks: The test enables one of two interrupt lines based on build configuration and uses a global pending flag to release wait loops. Input levels are stimulated via a memory-mapped location.

2) For each GPIO pin from 8 to 39, configure the per‑pin control register (GPIO_8 block with per‑pin offset) for input mode with level‑triggered interrupt (active high).
3) Enable the corresponding group interrupt for the selected pin using gp0_intr2_intr_en1.
4) Write 0xFFFFFFFF to 0xA0243ffc to assert the input level and wait until the pending flag is cleared by the interrupt handler.
5) Repeat steps 2–4 for active‑low level selection (configure per‑pin control for active‑low level, enable the group interrupt for that pin, write the complement pattern to 0xA0243ffc to drive a low level for that pin, and wait for the interrupt).
6) In the interrupt handler, verify the per‑pin raw interrupt status via the per‑pin register (GPIO_8 block), then verify the group status bit in INTR1_INTR_STS1.
7) Clear the per‑pin raw interrupt status in the per‑pin register and verify the group status is cleared in INTR1_INTR_STS1 after disabling the group enable.
8) Clear the system raw interrupt status in RAW_STCR1 for the active GPIO instance and confirm the status is cleared.
9) Clear the CPU interrupt line for the active GPIO instance.

- When configured for active‑high level, an asserted level causes the per‑pin raw interrupt status to indicate an interrupt; pass if set, otherwise fail.
- The corresponding group interrupt status bit in INTR1_INTR_STS1 is set for the active pin; pass if set, otherwise fail.
- After clearing the per‑pin raw status and disabling the group enable, the per‑pin status indicates cleared and the group status in INTR1_INTR_STS1 is 0; pass if cleared, otherwise fail.
- The system raw interrupt status for the selected GPIO instance is cleared in RAW_STCR1 after the clear operation; pass if cleared, otherwise fail.
- If no raw interrupt is indicated when expected, the handler reports an error and the test fails.

Feature: interrupts can be generated based on positive edge or negative edge or level high or level low detection at GPIO input
Test Description: Validates negative-edge interrupt generation on even-numbered GPIO pads. Confirms input state, raw and group interrupt status, and proper clearing.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Initialize the test and enable the CPU interrupt line for the active GPIO instance.
2) Enable the system interrupt for the active GPIO instance.
3) For each GPIO from 8 to 39, configure per‑pin control for negative‑edge interrupt.
4) Configure the group control registers so that GPIOs 8–39 are in input mode with negative‑edge interrupt selection.
5) Enable group interrupt for all pins in the first interrupt group.
6) For each GPIO index i from 0 to 31: if i is even, set the pending flag, drive all inputs high, wait briefly, then drive only bit i low to create a falling edge and wait for the interrupt to occur.
7) In the interrupt service routine, verify the input state for the active pin, confirm the per‑pin raw interrupt is set, confirm the group status bit is set, clear the per‑pin raw interrupt, verify per‑pin readback shows cleared, verify the group status is cleared, and clear the system raw status for the active GPIO instance.
8) Clear the CPU interrupt line and finish the test with the accumulated error count.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
- Input state verification: During the interrupt, the input state of the active pin must read as asserted; pass if asserted, otherwise fail.
- Raw interrupt status: The per‑pin raw status for the active pin must indicate a negative‑edge event; pass if set, otherwise fail.
- Group interrupt status set: The group interrupt status bit for the active pin must be set during the event; pass if set, otherwise fail.

Test Description: Validates negative-edge interrupt generation and handling for randomly selected GPIO pads. Confirms input state, raw and group interrupt status, and proper interrupt clearing.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Enable the CPU interrupt line for the active GPIO instance.
2) Enable the system interrupt for the active GPIO instance.
3) For each iteration, select a new pad number not used before and configure the per-pad control in gp0_intr2_intr_en1 for input mode with negative-edge trigger.
4) Enable the corresponding group interrupt bit in INTR1_INTR_EN1 for the selected pad.
5) Drive a falling edge for the selected pad by writing the inverted single-bit pattern to 0xA0243ffc, then restore the level to high.
6) Wait for the interrupt to occur.

8) Read INTR1_INTR_STS1 and verify the group status bit for the pad is set.
9) Disable the group enable in INTR1_INTR_EN1 and clear the per-pad raw status; verify the per-pad readback shows the interrupt cleared.
10) Read INTR1_INTR_STS1 and verify the group status is cleared.
11) Clear the system raw interrupt and then clear the CPU interrupt line.
12) Repeat the procedure for additional randomly selected, non-duplicate pads and finish with the final error count.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
- Per-pad input state: During handling of the event, the input state for the selected pad reads as asserted; pass if asserted, otherwise fail.

- Group status set: The group interrupt status shows the selected pad bit set; pass if set, otherwise fail.
- Per-pad clear: After clearing the per-pad raw status, the per-pad readback shows the interrupt cleared; pass if cleared, otherwise fail.
- Group status clear: After servicing, the group status reads as cleared; pass if zero, otherwise fail.
- System and CPU interrupt clear: The system raw status is cleared and the CPU interrupt line is cleared; pass if both are cleared, otherwise fail.
